subject: Proposal: Convert Retainer -> Commit with Step Change + Ramp Credit
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@latticeforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-10-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: Convert Retainer -> Commit with Step Change + Ramp Credit

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, LatticeForge is planning a mid-term capacity increase (additional 500k token-hours over the next 3 months) and wants price predictability while they accelerate feature rollout. Attached is a short proposal that does two things:

- Converts your existing $75k/month retainer into a staged committed volume for the next 12 months (Commit floor = 9M token-hours/year).
- Applies a one-time "onramp credit" that offsets month 1 and month 2 overages to smooth the transition (see attached schedule).

Key commercial highlights:
- Effective blended rate after credits: 12% lower than current list for the first 3 months.
- We can hold current rate (price-hold) for 90 days post-signature for the committed baseline.
- Option to tier down spike pricing if usage is sustained above 70% of the new commit for two consecutive months.

Two asks from your side to finalize: confirmation of the uplift cadence (immediate vs phased start) and a contact for procurement to accept the term-sheet.

I copied Marissa to confirm invoicing cadence and Marcus to confirm capacity sizing/latency SLOs for the uplift. If that sounds reasonable I can circulate a DocuSign copy of the term sheet and a short Ops runbook.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise GTM — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: LF_Onramp_Credit_Schedule_v1.pdf (1 page, table), Commit_Conversion_TermSheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@latticeforge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LatticeForge Procurement <procurement@latticeforge.com>
Date: 2028-10-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Convert Retainer -> Commit with Step Change + Ramp Credit

Thanks Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear schedule. A few notes from our side: 

1) We can commit to the baseline convert but need the 90-day price-hold to cover an upcoming procurement review.
2) Procurement (copied) prefers net-30 invoicing; can Marissa confirm if that aligns?
3) Two technical asks for Marcus: can you confirm the projected p95 latency with the additional KV cache allocation and whether the ramp will trigger any model variant fallbacks?

If the above aligns we can sign the term sheet next week. Also asking if Redwood can extend the onramp credit to cover Month 3 at a reduced level (50% of month 1 credit) — that would smooth our internal runway.

Cheers,
Dana
Dana Liu
Head of ML Platform — LatticeForge
dana.liu@latticeforge.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-10-18T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: Convert Retainer -> Commit with Step Change + Ramp Credit

Ben — copying internal notes for approval routing and cashflow impact.

On procurement terms: net-30 is fine, we will need to add the usual invoice credit description for the onramp adjustment so G&A recognizes the timing. I'll flag estimated revenue recognition impact with finance (approx deferral of ~$95k recognition into Q4).

On Dana's ask to extend Month 3 at 50% credit: I'd be comfortable approving a 50% third-month onramp credit if the committed floor increases by at least 15% vs the draft. That keeps our unit economics covered. 

Marcus — can you confirm the ops validation (p95 expected and fallback behavior)? If Marcus gives a green light I will prepare an approval note for the CRO with the suggested concession (50% Month3 credit + +15% commit uplift).

- Marissa

Forwarded message:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@latticeforge.com>
Subject: Re: Proposal...
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dana Liu <dana.liu@latticeforge.com>
Date: 2028-10-19T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Convert Retainer -> Commit with Step Change + Ramp Credit

Hi all — quick ops note: we validated the KV cache bump and routing rules in staging. Expect p95 inference latency to increase ~4-6ms under the projected uplift (well within your SLA target). We have a model-variant fallback configured (lighter quantized variant) that would trigger only if instance queue depth crosses 85% across a single AZ — that fallback is compatible with the commit rates in the term sheet but may be slightly higher-cost for short durations.

Operational recommendation: accept the 50% Month 3 onramp credit if LatticeForge increases the committed floor by 15% (as Marissa suggested). That trade-off preserves our margin for sustained usage and reduces financial risk for Redwood. I'll attach a short ops-runbook after signature.

Ben — if you want, I can add a short bulleted appendix to the term sheet that calls out the fallback behavior and expected latency uplift.

Marcus
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
